mainTopic: Relatives forbidden after חליצה: whether שניות apply to a חלוצה, and the status of the חלוצה's צרה
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a man who did חליצה with his יבמה. The חכמים treat her somewhat like his wife: he may not marry her close relatives, and she may not marry his close relatives, but the other brothers are not affected. The גמרא then asks whether the חכמים also forbade the more distant relatives (שניות) of a חלוצה, as they did for a real wife. Several proofs from the משנה and from a ברייתא of רבי חייא are pushed off, because each ban could come from her real marriage to the dead brother. Finally, the case of the חולץ's daughter's son cannot be explained that way, so the גמרא concludes that the חכמים did decree שניות for a חלוצה. The גמרא then turns to the חלוצה's צרה (co-wife). שמואל rules that a child from her is a ממזר, and רב יוסף supports him from the משנה. רבי יוחנן escapes that proof, because a חלוצה's sister is forbidden only by the rabbis. The amud ends by asking why the משנה permits a relative of the צרה but forbids a צרה of the relative, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The man who did חליצה may not marry her close relatives
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the חלוצה's relatives who are forbidden to the man who did חליצה. It adds that the other brothers are not affected.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is forbidden to her mother, her mother's mother, her father's mother, her daughter, her daughter's daughter, her son's daughter, and her sister while she is alive. The other brothers are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists which of the חלוצה's relatives the man who did חליצה may not marry. The other brothers, who did not do חליצה, may marry them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After חליצה the חכמים treat the חלוצה somewhat like his wife, so her relatives are forbidden to him the same way a wife's relatives would be. As with a wife's sister, her sister is forbidden only while she is alive. This applies only to the brother who actually did חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
The woman who went through חליצה
Close relatives, here the ones he may not marry
While she is still alive
The other brothers of the deceased

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that חליצה creates a wife-like link only for the one brother who performs it.

phrases.english: He is forbidden to her mother,
and to her mother's mother, and to her father's mother,
and to her daughter, and to her daughter's daughter, and to her son's daughter,
and to her sister while she is alive.
But the brothers are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from before this section about the status of a man who did חליצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man who did חליצה is forbidden to the חלוצה's close relatives (her sister only during her lifetime). The other brothers are permitted to them.

steps.title: The חלוצה may not marry his close relatives
steps.stepSummary: The prohibition works in both directions: the חלוצה is forbidden to the close male relatives of the man who did חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she is forbidden to his father, his father's father, his son, his son's son, his brother, and his brother's son.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the other direction: she may not marry his close relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as a wife may not marry her husband's father or son, the חלוצה may not marry the father, son and similar relatives of the man who did חליצה. The list mirrors the relatives a woman cannot marry after being married to someone.

keyTerms.meaning: She is forbidden
His father's father
His son's son
His brother's son

phrases.english: And she is forbidden to his father, and to his father's father,
and to his son, and to his son's son,
to his brother, and to his brother's son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror image of step 1: her prohibitions toward his relatives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חלוצה is forbidden to the father, grandfather, son, grandson, brother and nephew of the man who did חליצה.

steps.title: Relative of the צרה permitted, צרה of the relative forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה contrasts two cases that sound alike: a relative of the חלוצה's צרה is permitted, but a צרה of the חלוצה's relative is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man is permitted to a relative of the צרה of his חלוצה, but forbidden to the צרה of a relative of his חלוצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a final rule that turns on word order: "relative of the צרה" versus "צרה of the relative."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צרה was released through his חליצה with the other wife, but she is not considered his own חלוצה, so her relatives stay permitted. A relative of his חלוצה is forbidden to him, and that ban reaches her צרה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A rival wife, another wife of the same husband
A relative of his חלוצה's rival wife
A rival wife of his חלוצה's relative

steps.confusionAlert: The two phrases use the same words in reverse order. Read slowly: the first is the צרה's relative (permitted), the second is the relative's צרה (forbidden).
steps.whatToRemember: After חליצה, he is bound to her relatives and she to his. Only the brother who did חליצה is affected. Her צרה's relatives stay permitted, but the צרות of her relatives are forbidden.

phrases.english: A man is permitted to the relative of the rival wife of his חלוצה.
But he is forbidden to the rival wife of the relative of his חלוצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final contrast that sharpens how far the prohibition from step 1 reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A relative of the חלוצה's צרה is permitted to him; a צרה of the חלוצה's relative is forbidden.

steps.title: Did the חכמים forbid secondary relatives of a חלוצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking whether the rabbinic ban on a wife's שניות (more distant relatives) also applies to a חלוצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A question was asked: did they decree שניות for a חלוצה, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion with an open question, setting up the debate that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a real wife, the חכמים added a ban on certain more distant relatives (שניות) beyond the Torah's list. Since the חכמים already treat a חלוצה somewhat like a wife, the question is whether they went further and applied the שניות ban to her too.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
"It was asked of them"; introduces an open question
They (the חכמים) decreed
Secondary relatives, forbidden only by the חכמים

steps.whyThisMatters: It tests how far the rabbinic comparison of a חלוצה to a wife actually reaches.

phrases.english: Gemara
A question was asked of them:
Did they decree secondary relatives for a חלוצה, or not?
phrases.notes: For a real wife, the חכמים also forbade some more distant relatives. Did they do that for a חלוצה too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the משנה's rule that her close relatives are forbidden and asks whether the ban reaches further.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rabbinic ban on שניות applies to the relatives of a חלוצה, as it does to a wife's relatives.

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out both possibilities: maybe שניות were decreed only for Torah-level עריות and not for a חלוצה, or maybe there is no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did the רבנן decree a ban on secondary relatives only for a real Torah-level forbidden relationship, and not for a חלוצה? Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the question it began in the previous step by laying out the two sides. This sets up the attempted proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a real wife, her close relatives are forbidden by the Torah, so the רבנן added a 'fence' of more distant relatives (שניות). A חלוצה's relatives are forbidden only by the רבנן to begin with. The question is whether the רבנן would build a second fence around a rule that is already rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden relationship from the Torah itself
The Sages made a decree
'Secondary' relatives, forbidden only by the רבנן
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
There is no difference

phrases.english: In a case of a Torah-level forbidden relationship,
the Sages decreed secondary relatives for them,
but for a חלוצה the Sages did not decree secondary relatives?
Or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question opened in step 4 by stating both sides.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the שניות decree reaches the relatives of a חלוצה, whose own prohibition is only rabbinic.

steps.title: Proof from what the משנה leaves out
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the חלוצה's mother and grandmother but not her great-grandmother. This suggests there is no שניות ban for a חלוצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: he is forbidden to her mother and her mother's mother, but the משנה does not list her mother's mother's mother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from our own משנה. It points out that the משנה stops at the grandmother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The great-grandmother is a classic example of a שניה. Since the משנה lists the closer relatives and skips her, it seems the man who did חליצה may marry her. That would mean no שניות ban applies to a חלוצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Her mother's mother's mother, her great-grandmother
It does not teach / does not list

phrases.english: Come and hear:
He is forbidden to her mother and to her mother's mother,
whereas 'her mother's mother's mother' it does not teach!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question from step 5 using the משנה's list.
steps.raayaObject: That no שניות decree applies to a חלוצה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's list stops at the grandmother and leaves out the great-grandmother.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה stopped early for another reason
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. Had the משנה listed the great-grandmother, one might think 'the brothers are permitted' applies only to her and not to the closer relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this is why it doesn't list her: because it wants to teach in the last part, 'and the brothers are permitted.' If it had listed 'her mother's mother's mother,' I would have thought the brothers are permitted only to the great-grandmother, but not to her mother's mother or her mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by giving a different reason the משנה left out the great-grandmother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last part of the משנה says the other brothers are permitted to all these relatives. If the list had ended with the great-grandmother, a reader might link 'the brothers are permitted' only to that last, most distant relative. So silence about the great-grandmother does not prove she is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
The last part of the משנה
I would have thought (a mistaken assumption)
Specifically, only

phrases.english: Perhaps this is the reason it does not teach it,
because it wants to teach in the last part
'and the brothers are permitted,'
and if it had taught 'her mother's mother's mother,'
I would have thought: the brothers are permitted
only to her mother's mother's mother,
but to her mother's mother and her mother, not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 6 by explaining the משנה's silence differently.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the inference from the missing great-grandmother. It does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The omission could be about clear wording for the brothers' clause, not about the law of the great-grandmother.

steps.title: Why not list her and say 'permitted to all of them'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the push-off: the משנה could have listed the great-grandmother and then said 'the brothers are permitted to all of them.' The challenge is left as a difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let it teach 'her mother's mother's mother,' and let it teach 'the brothers are permitted to all of them'! It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from the previous step and ends with the word קשיא, meaning 'this is a difficulty.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about misreading could easily be fixed by adding 'to all of them.' Since the משנה didn't do that, the omission again suggests the great-grandmother is truly permitted, which brings back the proof from step 6. The גמרא admits the difficulty but does not treat it as decisive, and it keeps looking for proof (steps 9-29).

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it teach (a challenge: the משנה could have said it)
To all of them
It is a difficulty (left without an answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list stops at the חלוצה's grandmother. The attempt to explain that away ends with a קשיא, so this proof points toward no שניות for a חלוצה. It does not decide the question: the גמרא keeps looking, and step 29 concludes the opposite, that the חכמים did decree שניות for a חלוצה.
steps.confusionAlert: Here קַשְׁיָא means the push-off in step 7 is hard to defend. It is not a final ruling. In fact, the גמרא's conclusion in step 29 goes the other way: the חכמים did apply שניות to a חלוצה.

phrases.english: But let it teach 'her mother's mother's mother,'
and let it teach 'the brothers are permitted to all of them'!
It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the push-off in step 7 and leaves it as an unanswered difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation in step 7 that the great-grandmother was left out to avoid misreading the brothers' clause.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Adding the word 'בְּכוּלָּן' would have removed the misreading, so the worry does not explain why the great-grandmother is missing.

steps.title: Proof from the ban on the grandfather
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says she is forbidden to the חולץ's father's father. The גמרא suggests this is because the חליצה makes her count as the grandfather's grandson's wife, which is a שניות ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'She is forbidden to his father and to his father's father.' At least it teaches 'his father's father.' Isn't this because of the חולץ, since that makes her his son's daughter-in-law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof from the משנה. It says she is forbidden to the חולץ's grandfather, and this seems to be a שניות ban that comes from the חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a grandson's wife is a שניה, a rabbinic ban, not a Torah one. If the grandfather is forbidden because of the חולץ, then חליצה does create שניות bans. That would answer the question from step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches; it points to the one detail being used as proof
Is it not...? It suggests the reading that gives a proof
The brother who performed חליצה
His son's daughter-in-law, meaning his grandson's wife

phrases.english: Come and hear:
She is forbidden to his father and to his father's father.
phrases.notes: This is a line from our משנה. 'His' means the brother who did חליצה with her.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches 'his father's father';
is it not because of the one who did חליצה,
since she counts as his son's daughter-in-law!
phrases.notes: The grandfather's son's daughter-in-law is his grandson's wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הִיא אֲסוּרָה בְּאָבִיו וּבַאֲבִי אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in steps 6-8 was left as a difficulty, the גמרא tries another proof from the same משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That שניות bans apply to a חלוצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ban on the חולץ's father's father

steps.title: The grandfather ban comes from the dead husband
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The grandfather is also the dead husband's grandfather, so she really was his grandson's wife through her actual marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is because of the dead husband, through whom she is his son's daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ban on the grandfather may come from her real marriage to the dead brother, not from the חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חולץ and the dead husband are brothers, so they share the same grandfather. She actually was married to that grandfather's grandson, the dead husband. So the ban needs no help from the חליצה, and nothing is proven about חלוצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead one, meaning her late husband

phrases.english: No, it is because of the dead husband,
since through him she counts as his son's daughter-in-law.
phrases.notes: The dead husband is the grandfather's grandson too, so she really was his grandson's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the proof of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only this proof is rejected. The question itself is decided later, in step 29.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban on the grandfather can be explained by her actual marriage to the dead husband, so it does not show that חליצה creates שניות.

steps.title: Proof from the ban on the grandson
steps.stepSummary: The משנה also forbids her to the חולץ's grandson. The גמרא suggests this is because the חליצה makes her count as the grandson's grandfather's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And to his son's son.' Isn't this because of the חולץ, since that makes her the wife of his father's father?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof from the next part of the same משנה. This time the relative is the חולץ's grandson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To the חולץ's grandson, the חולץ is his grandfather. If the חליצה makes her count as the חולץ's wife, she is the grandson's grandfather's wife, which is a שניה. If that is the reason for the ban, then חליצה does create שניות.

keyTerms.meaning: His son's son, meaning his grandson
The wife of his father's father, meaning his grandfather's wife

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'And to his son's son.'
phrases.notes: Another line from our משנה: she is also forbidden to the חולץ's grandson.

phrases.english: Is it not because of the one who did חליצה,
since she counts as the wife of his father's father!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. Either way, the meaning stays the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the grandfather proof was pushed off, the גמרא tries a parallel proof from the grandson.
steps.raayaObject: That שניות bans apply to a חלוצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ban on the חולץ's son's son

steps.title: The grandson ban also comes from the dead husband
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. Through her real marriage to the dead husband, she is the wife of the grandson's grandfather's brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is because of the dead husband, through whom she is the wife of his father's father's brother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects this proof the same way it rejected the last one. The ban can come from her real marriage to the dead husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dead husband is the brother of the חולץ, who is the grandson's grandfather. So she actually was married to the grandson's great-uncle, and that is a forbidden relationship on its own. Again the ban does not depend on the חליצה, so the question of step 4 is not settled yet; step 29 settles it.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of his grandfather's brother, meaning his great-uncle's wife

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs fail for the same reason. Any ban that the משנה lists might come from her actual marriage to the dead husband, so it cannot show that חליצה by itself creates שניות.

phrases.english: No, it is because of the dead husband,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוְיָא לַהּ אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי אֲבִי אָבִיו.
phrases.english: and through him she counts as the wife of his father's father's brother.
phrases.notes: The dead husband is the brother of the grandson's grandfather (the חולץ), so he is the grandson's great-uncle.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מִשּׁוּם מִיתָנָא, וְהָוְיָא לַהּ אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי אֲבִי אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the proof of step 11, using the same move as step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the grandson proof is rejected. The main question is decided later, in step 29.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The grandson's ban can come from her real marriage to his great-uncle, the dead husband, and not from the חליצה.

steps.title: אמימר Permits a Great-Uncle's Wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to Step 12's push-off: אמימר rules that a man may marry the wife of his father's father's brother, so that relationship cannot explain why the משנה forbids her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But אמימר permits marrying the wife of one's father's father's brother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the push-off from Step 12. It points out that אמימר allows a man to marry his grandfather's brother's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the grandson is forbidden to her because she was the wife of his grandfather's brother. אמימר holds that this relationship is not forbidden at all, not even by rabbinic law. So the push-off seems to fail, and the ban would have to come from the חליצה after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Permits, rules it allowed
The wife of one's father's father's brother (a great-uncle's wife)

phrases.english: But אמימר permits
phrases.notes: This is aimed at Step 12, which said the grandson is forbidden to her because she was his great-uncle's wife.

phrases.english: the wife of his father's father's brother!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the push-off of Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The push-off in Step 12 that the ban comes from her being the great-uncle's wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אמימר permits a great-uncle's wife, so that relationship cannot be the source of a ban.

steps.title: אמימר Reads 'His Son's Son' as the Grandfather's Grandson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that אמימר understands the משנה's 'his son's son' as referring to the grandson of the grandfather, not the grandson of the חולץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר explains it as referring to the grandfather's grandson.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the push-off by saying אמימר reads the משנה differently. To him, 'his son's son' means the grandfather's grandson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'his' in 'his son's son' could point back to the חולץ or to the grandfather mentioned just before it. אמימר takes it as the grandfather. Then the משנה is not talking about the חולץ's grandson at all, so there is no proof that חליצה creates a new ban.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets it up as, explains it as referring to
A son's son, a grandson
Grandfather

steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement here is only about who 'his' refers to in the משנה. Read it as the grandfather, not the חולץ, and the whole case changes.

phrases.english: אמימר establishes it
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's words 'his son's son.'

phrases.english: as the son of the son of the grandfather.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'His son's son' means the חולץ's grandson, which would only be a rabbinic ban created by the חליצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For אמימר, 'his son's son' means the grandfather's grandson, so no proof can be drawn from it.

steps.title: Then the משנה Repeats the Brother and Nephew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if the משנה means the grandfather's sons and grandsons, those are just the brother and the brother's son, which the משנה already lists.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, these are the same as his brother and his brother's son!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אמימר's reading. It says that reading makes the משנה repeat relatives it already named.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under אמימר's reading, the relatives in this part of the משנה turn out to be people already listed as 'his brother and his brother's son.' A משנה does not normally repeat itself for no reason, so the reading seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
That is the same as
His brother and his brother's son

phrases.english: If so,
that is the same as his brother and his brother's son!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ אָחִיו וּבֶן אָחִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's reading of 'his son's son' as the grandfather's grandson
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes the משנה repeat relatives it already listed.

steps.title: Paternal Brother and Maternal Brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there is no repetition: the משנה first teaches a brother from the father, and then teaches a brother from the mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: It taught his brother from the father, and then it teaches his brother from the mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves אמימר's reading. The two listings are not the same people, because one is a paternal brother and the other is a maternal brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first mention of 'his brother' covers a brother sharing the same father. The second listing, read אמימר's way, adds a brother sharing only the same mother. So each phrase teaches something new, and the משנה is not repeating itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught
His brother from the father (paternal half-brother)
His brother from the mother (maternal half-brother)

steps.whatToRemember: The proofs from the משנה's list of his relatives (steps 9-16) have all been pushed off. That part of the משנה can be read so that every ban comes from her real marriage to the dead husband, not from the חליצה.

phrases.english: It taught his brother from the father,
and then it teaches his brother from the mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא אָחִיו מִן הָאָב, וְקָתָנֵי אָחִיו מִן הָאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that each phrase teaches a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second listing repeats the brother and nephew already mentioned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first listing is the paternal brother and the second is the maternal brother, so nothing is repeated.

steps.title: רבי חייא's List: Four from the Torah, Four from the Rabbis
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new attempted proof from a ברייתא of רבי חייא, which lists four relatives forbidden to a חלוצה by Torah law and four by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear what רבי חייא taught: four are from Torah law and four from rabbinic law. The father, his son, his brother, and his brother's son are from Torah law. His father's father, his mother's father, his son's son, and his daughter's son are from rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attempted proof by quoting רבי חייא's list. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will use the list to address the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list splits the relatives into two groups. The father, son, brother and nephew are forbidden by the Torah. The two grandfathers and two grandsons are forbidden only by the rabbis.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law
By rabbinic law
His mother's father
His daughter's son

phrases.english: Come and hear, for רבי חייא taught:
Four are from the words of the Torah,
and four are from the words of the Rabbis:
the father and his son, his brother, and his brother's son —
from the words of the Torah.
His father's father, and his mother's father,
his son's son, and his daughter's son —
from the words of the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs from the משנה were pushed off, the גמרא tries a new source
steps.raayaObject: Whether חליצה itself creates rabbinic bans (שניות)
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי חייא listing four Torah-level and four rabbinic-level relatives

steps.title: Proof from the grandfather on the father's side
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists 'his father's father' as forbidden. The גמרא suggests this is because of the חולץ, which would make her the grandfather's son's daughter-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches that she is forbidden to his father's father. Isn't that because of the חולץ, which makes her his son's daughter-in-law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks one item from רבי חייא's list, the father's father, and tries to use it as proof that the חולץ's relatives count as שניות for the חלוצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son's daughter-in-law is a rabbinic secondary relative. If the grandfather is forbidden to her because of her link to the חולץ, then חליצה creates a family tie strong enough to bring in שניות. That is exactly the point being tested.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches. This points to one detail in a source to prove something.
Is it not? This opens a suggested reading that would prove the point.
The brother who performed חליצה with the widow
His son's daughter-in-law, a rabbinic secondary relative
His father's father (the grandfather)

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches: his father's father.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא of רבי חייא from the step before. 'His' refers to the brothers, the חולץ and the deceased.

phrases.english: Is it not because of the one who performed חליצה,
so that she is his son's daughter-in-law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a specific item from the ברייתא introduced in Step 17
steps.raayaObject: That שניות apply to a חלוצה through her tie to the חולץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא listing 'father's father' among the rabbinic prohibitions

steps.title: The grandfather is forbidden because of the deceased brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. She is the grandfather's son's daughter-in-law because she was really married to the deceased, who is also his grandson.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is because of the deceased husband, since through him she is his son's daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by giving a different reason for the grandfather's prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deceased and the חולץ are brothers from the same father, so the grandfather is the deceased's father's father too. She really was married to the deceased, so she really is the grandfather's son's daughter-in-law through that marriage. The ברייתא's ruling proves nothing about the חליצה link.

keyTerms.meaning: The deceased, the brother who died and was really married to her
No. This opens a rejection of the suggested proof.

phrases.english: No, it is because of the deceased,
for through him she is his son's daughter-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 18
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The prohibition can be explained by her real marriage to the deceased, so it does not show that the חולץ link creates שניות

steps.title: Proof from the grandfather on the mother's side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries again with 'his mother's father' from the same list. It suggests he is forbidden because of the חולץ, which would make her his daughter's daughter-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: his mother's father. Isn't that because of the חולץ, which makes her his daughter's daughter-in-law?
steps.whatsHappening: The first proof failed, so the גמרא moves to the next item on רבי חייא's list and tries the same kind of proof again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A daughter's daughter-in-law is also a rabbinic secondary relative. If the mother's father is forbidden because of her link to the חולץ, then חליצה would create שניות.

keyTerms.meaning: His mother's father (the grandfather on the mother's side)
His daughter's daughter-in-law, a rabbinic secondary relative

phrases.english: Come and hear: his mother's father.
Is it not because of the one who performed חליצה,
for she is his daughter's daughter-in-law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 19 rejected the first proof, a new proof from the next item in the same ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That שניות apply to a חלוצה through her tie to the חולץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא listing 'mother's father'

steps.title: The mother's father is also forbidden because of the deceased
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off this proof the same way. She is the grandfather's daughter's daughter-in-law through her real marriage to the deceased.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is because of the deceased husband, since through him she is his daughter's daughter-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof with the same answer as before: the prohibition comes from the deceased, not from the חולץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother's father is the deceased's grandfather too, as when the brothers share the same mother. In that case the woman's real marriage to the deceased is enough to make her his daughter's daughter-in-law. So this item also fails to prove that חליצה creates שניות.

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary relatives, forbidden by rabbinic law
A widow who received חליצה
By rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: Both grandfathers on רבי חייא's list can be explained through the woman's real marriage to the deceased. So far, nothing proves that her חליצה link to the חולץ creates שניות.

phrases.english: No, it is because of the deceased,
for through him she is his daughter's daughter-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מִשּׁוּם מִיתָנָא, דְּהָוְיָא לַהּ כַּלַּת בִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 20 using the same answer as Step 19
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The prohibition can come from her real marriage to the deceased, so it does not show that the חולץ link creates שניות

steps.title: Trying a proof from 'his son's son'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא forbids the חלוצה to the חולץ's grandson (his son's son). The גמרא suggests this is because of the חולץ, which would make her the grandson's grandfather's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'and his son's son.' Isn't it because of the חולץ, since she would count as the wife of his father's father?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third case from the same ברייתא to try again to prove that שניות apply to a חלוצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we treat her as if she were married to the חולץ, then to the חולץ's grandson she is his grandfather's wife. That is a שניה. So if the ברייתא forbids her for this reason, the rabbis did apply שניות to a חלוצה.

keyTerms.meaning: His son's son (his grandson through his son)
The wife of his father's father (his grandfather's wife), a שניה

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'and his son's son.'
phrases.notes: 'His' means the חולץ, the brother who did חליצה. This is his grandson.

phrases.english: Isn't it because of the one who did חליצה,
since she would be the wife of his father's father!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two failed proofs from the grandfathers in the list, the גמרא turns to the grandsons.
steps.raayaObject: That the rabbis applied שניות to a חלוצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא listing 'his son's son' as forbidden

steps.title: No, it is because of the dead brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: the grandson is forbidden because of her real marriage to the deceased, which makes her his great-uncle's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is because of the dead husband, and she is the wife of his father's father's brother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof by giving a different reason why the grandson is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dead husband was the חולץ's brother, so to the חולץ's grandson he is a great-uncle. Her real marriage to him makes her the grandson's great-uncle's wife. So the ban could come from that marriage, not from the חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead one, meaning the brother who died
The wife of his father's father's brother (his great-uncle's wife)

phrases.english: No, it is because of the deceased,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָוְיָא לַהּ אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי אֲבִי אָבִיו.
phrases.english: and she is the wife of his father's father's brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 22 the same way steps 19 and 21 rejected the earlier proofs.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only this proof from 'his son's son'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban can be explained by her real marriage to the deceased, so the חליצה is not needed

steps.title: But אמימר permits a great-uncle's wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the pushback: אמימר holds that a great-uncle's wife is permitted, so the dead brother cannot be the reason for the ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: But אמימר permits the wife of one's father's father's brother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the pushback from step 23 by citing אמימר's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said she is forbidden as the great-uncle's wife. But אמימר rules that a great-uncle's wife is not forbidden at all. So according to אמימר, the pushback fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Permits, rules it is allowed

phrases.english: But אמימר permits
the wife of his father's father's brother!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַמֵּימָר מַכְשִׁיר בְּאֵשֶׁת אֲחִי אֲבִי אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the pushback of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 23 that the grandson is forbidden as the great-uncle's wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אמימר permits a great-uncle's wife, so that cannot be the source of the ban

steps.title: אמימר does read it as because of the חולץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: אמימר explains the case as because of the חולץ, so he must hold that the rabbis applied שניות to a חלוצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר explains it as because of the חולץ, and he holds that the rabbis decreed שניות for a חלוצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by admitting that, for אמימר, the proof works, because he really does hold that שניות apply to a חלוצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since אמימר can't use the great-uncle reason, he must say the ban comes from the חולץ. That only works if the rabbis applied שניות to a חלוצה. So the pushback in step 23 only works for people who disagree with אמימר, and the search for proof continues for them.

keyTerms.meaning: He explains it as being about
He holds, this is his view
The rabbis decreed the שניות bans for a חלוצה too

steps.whatToRemember: For אמימר, שניות do apply to a חלוצה. The גמרא now keeps looking for proof that works even for those who disagree with him, and step 29 finds it.

phrases.english: אמימר explains it as because of the חולץ,
and he holds that they decreed שניות for a חלוצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 24 by limiting the pushback to those who disagree with אמימר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope: the proof holds for אמימר, and the pushback holds only for those who disagree with him
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The pushback of step 23 seemed to work for everyone
steps.terutzMaskana: אמימר explains the case through the חולץ and holds that שניות apply to a חלוצה

steps.title: Trying a proof from 'his daughter's son'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא also forbids her to the חולץ's daughter's son. The גמרא suggests this is because of the חולץ, which would make her the grandson's mother's father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'and his daughter's son.' Isn't it because of the חולץ, since she would count as the wife of his mother's father?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a new proof, for those who disagree with אמימר, from the last grandson case in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is treated as the חולץ's wife, then to his daughter's son she is his mother's father's wife, which is a שניה. So the ban here would show that the rabbis applied שניות to a חלוצה.

keyTerms.meaning: His daughter's son (his grandson through his daughter)
The wife of his mother's father, a שניה

steps.confusionAlert: Each case has two possible reasons for the ban: her being treated as the חולץ's wife (which needs שניות for a חלוצה), or her real marriage to the dead brother (which does not). Every proof asks which reason the ברייתא means.

phrases.english: Come and hear: 'and to his daughter's son.'
Isn't it because of the one who did חליצה,
since she would be the wife of his mother's father!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling אמימר's view, the גמרא keeps looking for proof for those who disagree with him.
steps.raayaObject: That the rabbis applied שניות to a חלוצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא listing 'his daughter's son' as forbidden

steps.title: Maybe the dead brother is the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof. Maybe the daughter's son is forbidden because of the woman's marriage to the dead brother, not because of the חולץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. She is forbidden because of the dead man. Through him she is the wife of the brother of the boy's mother's father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 26. It offers another reason why the חלוצה is forbidden to the חולץ's daughter's son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dead husband was the brother of the חולץ. The חולץ is the boy's mother's father. So the dead husband is the boy's great-uncle, and she is his great-uncle's wife. If that is the reason she is forbidden, we learn nothing about the חולץ.

keyTerms.meaning: The dead one: here, the brother who died
The wife of his mother's father's brother: a great-uncle's wife

phrases.english: No, it is because of the deceased,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוְיָא לַהּ אֵשֶׁת אֲחִי אֲבִי אִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: for she is the wife of his mother's father's brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 26 by offering a different source for the ban.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the daughter's son case, not the ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban could come from her real marriage to the dead brother, so it does not have to come from the חולץ.

steps.title: The rabbis never banned this relationship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the pushback. A mother's father's brother's wife is not one of the rabbinic שניות, so the dead brother cannot be the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the rabbis did not include this case among the secondary forbidden relationships!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the pushback from Step 27. That relationship is not on the list of rabbinic bans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great-uncle's wife on the mother's side is not one of the שניות the rabbis made. So the dead brother gives no reason to forbid her to this grandson. The pushback falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary relationships: extra family bans the rabbis added beyond the Torah ones
A Torah-forbidden relationship
They (the rabbis) decreed

phrases.english: But regarding the secondary relationships of forbidden relatives,
they did not decree this one!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא גַּבֵּי שְׁנִיּוֹת דְּעֶרְוָה לֹא גָּזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the pushback in Step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the dead brother explains the ban.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That relationship is not a rabbinic שניה, so the dead brother cannot create any ban here.

steps.title: Proven: the rabbis applied שניות to a חלוצה
steps.stepSummary: Since the dead brother cannot explain it, the reason must be the חולץ. This proves that the rabbis applied שניות to a חלוצה, and the גמרא accepts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it because of the חולץ? Learn from this that they decreed שניות for a חלוצה. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its first explanation and confirms the proof. The rabbis treated the חלוצה as if she were married to the חולץ, even for שניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the dead brother ruled out, only the חולץ is left as the reason for the ban. Through him she is the boy's mother's father's wife, which is a שניה. So the rabbis' ban on שניות does reach a חלוצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? (brings back the earlier explanation)
Learn from it: the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: The rabbis treated a חלוצה like the חולץ's wife, so the ban on שניות applies to her too. The proof comes from the case of the חולץ's daughter's son.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not because of the one who performed חליצה,
and learn from this that they decreed secondary relationships for a חלוצה?
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion after the pushback in Step 27 failed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rabbis applied the ban on שניות to a חלוצה, treating her as related to the חולץ.

steps.title: שמואל: the child of a צרת חלוצה is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה, which says a man may marry a relative of his חלוצה's co-wife. Through רב טובי בר קיסנא, שמואל rules that a child born from relations with a צרת חלוצה is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said, 'A man is permitted, etc.' רב טובי בר קיסנא said in the name of שמואל: if someone has relations with the co-wife of a חלוצה, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a ruling from שמואל about the co-wife of a חלוצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only one wife does חליצה, but the dead brother may have had other wives. שמואל says that after the חליצה, a co-wife is fully forbidden to the brother. That is a כרת-level ban, so a child born from it is a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The co-wife of the woman who received חליצה
A child born from a כרת-level forbidden relationship
One who has relations with

phrases.english: The משנה said: 'A man is permitted, etc.'
phrases.notes: The משנה line is: a man may marry a relative of his חלוצה's co-wife.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Tovi bar Kisna said in the name of Shmuel:
One who has relations with the co-wife of a חלוצה,
the child is a ממזר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child born from the co-wife of a חלוצה and the brother is a ממזר.

steps.title: Why: she goes back to her original ban
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for שמואל's reason. The answer is that the co-wife stays under her original Torah ban of a brother's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? She stands in her original prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains שמואל's ruling. The co-wife goes back to the full ban of a brother's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חליצה removed the ייבום bond. The co-wife was not part of that חליצה, so she does not get the lighter status of a חלוצה. She returns to the full ban of אשת אח, which carries כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
She stands in her original prohibition

phrases.english: What is the reason?
She remains in her original prohibition.
phrases.notes: Her original ban is the Torah ban on marrying a brother's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for שמואל's ruling in Step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the child of a צרת חלוצה is a ממזר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The co-wife goes back to the full Torah ban of a brother's wife.

steps.title: רב יוסף begins a support from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the משנה supports שמואל. A man may marry his חלוצה's co-wife's sister, which fits well if the co-wife is 'outside' the חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: we also learned this. 'A man is permitted to a relative of his חלוצה's co-wife.' It makes sense if you say the co-wife is outside the חליצה; that is why he may marry her sister.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף starts building a proof for שמואל from the משנה. Here he shows how the משנה fits שמואל's view, setting up the second half of the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the co-wife is not part of the חליצה, she has no link to the חולץ like a חלוצה does. Then her relatives are not relatives of his חלוצה, so they are permitted. The 'בשלמא' (it works well) sets up a contrast with the other view, which will follow.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it: a source supporting the ruling
It works well if you say...
Outside: not included in the חליצה
A relative of

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: We too have learned this:
A man is permitted to a relative of his חלוצה's co-wife.
It works well if you say the co-wife is outside,
phrases.notes: 'Outside' means she was not part of the חליצה, so she does not get the חלוצה's status.

phrases.english: that is why he is permitted to her sister.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts bringing support from the משנה for שמואל's view in Steps 30-31.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's view that the co-wife is not included in the חליצה and goes back to her original ban.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting a relative of the חלוצה's co-wife.

steps.title: Finishing רב יוסף's proof: if the co-wife were like the חלוצה, her relatives would be forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף completes his proof. If the co-wife were treated like the חלוצה herself, her sister should be forbidden just like the חלוצה's sister. Since the משנה permits her, the co-wife must be outside the חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say a co-wife is treated like the חלוצה, why is he allowed to marry her relative?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף finishes his proof for שמואל. He shows that the other way of reading the משנה does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man may not marry his own חלוצה's sister. If the co-wife were counted as part of the חליצה, her sister should be forbidden too. The משנה allows it, so the co-wife is not covered by the חליצה and goes back to her original ban, just as שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: A co-wife, another wife of the same husband
A widow who was released from יבום through חליצה
Is similar to, is treated like
Why?

phrases.english: But if you say
that a co-wife is like the חלוצה herself,
why is he permitted to her relative?
phrases.notes: He means the co-wife's sister, whom the משנה allows the man to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ צָרָה כַּחֲלוּצָה דָּמְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of רב יוסף's proof begun in step 32
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that a צרת חלוצה stays under her Torah ban of a brother's wife
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה permitting a man to marry his חלוצה's co-wife's sister

steps.title: Does this disprove רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: If the co-wife stays under her old ban, this seems to refute רבי יוחנן. He holds that neither the חולץ nor his brothers get כרת for the חלוצה or for her co-wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we say this is a refutation of רבי יוחנן? He said that neither the one who did חליצה nor his brothers are liable to כרת, not for the חלוצה and not for her co-wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the proof against רבי יוחנן. It asks whether the משנה refutes his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says there is no כרת for the co-wife, which means she does not go back to her full Torah ban. That treats her as covered by the חליצה. But the משנה, as רב יוסף read it, shows she is outside the חליצה, which seems to clash with רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggested challenge
A refutation, a decisive objection
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for forbidden relations such as a brother's wife

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of רבי יוחנן,
who said: whether he or the brothers —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין לֹא עַל הַחֲלוּצָה כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: are not liable to כרת for the חלוצה,
nor to כרת for her co-wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the proof for שמואל as a challenge against רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that there is no כרת for a צרת חלוצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows the co-wife is outside the חליצה and goes back to her ban of a brother's wife, which would mean כרת. רבי יוחנן says there is no כרת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's answer: a חלוצה's sister is only forbidden by the rabbis
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the proof assumes the ban on a חלוצה's sister is from the Torah. ריש לקיש says it is only rabbinic, so the rabbis could limit it to the real חלוצה and not extend it to her co-wife's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן can say to you: Do you really think a חלוצה's sister is forbidden by the Torah? ריש לקיש said that here רבי taught that a divorcée's sister is forbidden by the Torah, but a חלוצה's sister is forbidden by the words of the rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends himself. He shows that the משנה does not really prove the co-wife is outside the חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's proof only works if the co-wife's sister would have to be forbidden once the co-wife counts like the חלוצה. But the ban on a חלוצה's sister is rabbinic, so the rabbis could apply it only to the woman who actually did חליצה. The co-wife can still count as covered by the חליצה, with no כרת, while her sister stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah
A divorcée
From the words of the scribes, meaning rabbinic law

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying the co-wife is outside the חליצה. He keeps his view that she is covered by it. He only explains why her sister can still be permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a proof built on a rabbinic ban is weak, because the rabbis can set the exact limits of their own decree.

phrases.english: רבי יוחנן can say to you:
And do you think a חלוצה's sister is forbidden by the Torah?
But didn't ריש לקיש say:
Here רבי taught
phrases.notes: He is pointing to a line in a nearby משנה, on the next daf.

phrases.english: a divorcée's sister is forbidden by the words of the Torah,
a חלוצה's sister is forbidden by the words of the rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְתִסְבְּרַאּ אֲחוֹת חֲלוּצָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן by weakening רב יוסף's proof
steps.terutzResolutionType: Undercuts the assumption behind the proof: the ban on a חלוצה's sister is rabbinic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the co-wife counts like the חלוצה, her sister must be forbidden, so the משנה proves she is outside the חליצה
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the ban on a חלוצה's sister is only rabbinic, the rabbis limited it to the real חלוצה. The משנה fits רבי יוחנן too.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה does not refute רבי יוחנן. Both שמואל and רבי יוחנן can explain it.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's proof supports שמואל, but רבי יוחנן escapes it. A חלוצה's sister is forbidden only by the rabbis, so they never extended that ban to the co-wife's sister.

steps.title: Why is one case in the משנה permitted and the other forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and asks why a relative of the חלוצה's co-wife is permitted, while a co-wife of the חלוצה's relative is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about this one, and what is different about that one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the wording of the משנה. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules differently on two cases that sound almost the same. A relative of the חלוצה's co-wife is permitted, but a co-wife of the חלוצה's relative is forbidden. The גמרא wants to know what makes them different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It asks for the reason behind two different rulings

phrases.english: What is different about this one,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the relative of the חלוצה's co-wife, whom the משנה permits.

phrases.english: and what is different about that one?
phrases.notes: "That one" is the co-wife of the חלוצה's relative, whom the משנה forbids.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הַאי, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שמואל and רבי יוחנן discussion and goes back to the משנה's two contrasting cases
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the משנה permits a relative of the חלוצה's co-wife but forbids a co-wife of the חלוצה's relative
